  mcycle (CSR 0xB00) and minstret (0xB02) into the vsim hart so cycle
  counts continue from QEMU1's drain. StateDrain.drain_with_passthrough
  freshly reads both unconditionally so the vsim phase's contribution
  survives into QEMU2. e2e.sh + CTest entry
  test_e2e_mcycle_monotonicity (handoff_roundtrip) assert strict
  monotonicity on the drain files (mcycle@624, minstret@632).
- Status: done

### F-T2.5 MMIO inside ROI

- Trigger: Workload calls `putchar`, touches UART/PLIC, accesses ROM,
  or hits aliased memory inside ROI.
- Breaks: Phase-5 interconnect watch (`hybrid_plan.md` Section 5) was
  never implemented. Writes to MMIO ranges either vanish or hit
  SimpleMemory as if they were RAM. QEMU2 device state desyncs from
  vsim's view.
- Source: `verilator/src/platform/interconnect.hpp` (no watch);
  `hybrid_plan.md` Phase 5
- Fix: Define a single allowlist of RAM + permitted-MMIO ranges in
  `src/platform/interconnect.hpp`. SimpleMemory::read/write checks
  every access against the allowlist; out-of-range aborts with a
  diagnostic logging the offending PC + address. Implements the
  Phase-5 interconnect watch.
- Status: not-started

## Tier 3 - Bug surfaces invisible to current suite

### F-T3.1 State-value opacity in icount / simpoint paths

- Trigger: Any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value during `--mode icount` (single window) or
  any stage of `--mode simpoint` (BBV profile -> per-phase drain ->
  archive/replay).
- Breaks: The icount and simpoint code paths only assert exit code +
  PC range. A wrong register value passes both.
- Source: `hsim` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`)
- Fix: After QEMU2 connects via gdbstub, issue a single `g` packet to
  read the full register file; parse and memcmp byte by byte against
  the corresponding fields in state.bin. Fail the run on mismatch.
- Status: not-started

### F-T3.2 Untested trigger-mode combinations

- Trigger: csr-entry + icount-exit; icount-entry + pc-exit; BBV-emit
  with simultaneous icount; etc. With 4 modes (csr/pc/icount/simpoint)
  the entry x exit matrix is 16 pairings; the suite tests csr+csr and
  pc+pc only.
- Breaks: Plugin or vsim bug in a cross-mode path is invisible until
  hit in production.
- Source: gap in `scripts/run_e2e.sh` mode coverage
- Fix: Parameterize `scripts/run_e2e.sh` with separate `ENTRY_MODE` and
  `EXIT_MODE` env vars (default = MODE if unset). Add a top-level
  `matrix` mode that iterates the cross-product across one canonical
  fixture, skipping pairings the plugin rejects up front.
- Status: not-started

### F-T3.3 Submodule version drift

- Trigger: Upstream QEMU 9.x changes TCG plugin ABI; vsim refactors
  the DM; SimPoint pinned to 17783e5 stays unmaintained.
- Breaks: Plugin silently produces wrong state, or fails to build,
  with no CI gate.
- Source: `.gitmodules`; no CI matrix against upstream snapshots
- Fix: Add `scripts/check_upstream_drift.sh` that, for each submodule,
  `git fetch`es the upstream remote and reports commits since the
  pinned SHA. Schedule a weekly CI job that runs the script and
  attaches the report to an auto-filed GitHub issue when non-empty.
- Status: not-started

### F-T3.4 vlenb mismatch silent

- Trigger: Fixture built with `--march=rv64gcv` for VLEN=512 (vlenb=64)
  runs on a vsim configured for VLEN=256 (vlenb=32) - or vice versa.
- Breaks: No cross-check that `vlenb_qemu == vlenb_vsim`. ResumeDriver
  reads only `vlenb` bytes of V-reg payload; upper bytes left as
  uninitialized scratch. Garbage in V regs.
- Source: gap in `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` and ABI
  validator
- Fix: At handoff entry, before any V transport, ResumeDriver reads
  the hart's `vlenb` CSR (0xC22) via Abstract Command and compares
  against `state.vlenb`. Mismatch aborts with a clear error naming
  both values. Same check on qemu_handback ingress side.
- Status: not-started

### F-T3.5 Failure-injection holes

- Trigger: Partial state drain mid-handoff; SIGKILL; disk full; mmap
  truncated to wrong size; corrupt magic with valid struct size.
- Breaks: Existing negative drivers cover only 4 scenarios
  (corrupt-state-short-read, no-qemu-binary, gdbstub-timeout,
  pty-handback). Subtle resource-exhaustion or race-condition paths
  unguarded.
- Source: `verilator/tests/hybrid/rt_{corrupt_state,no_qemu_binary,gdbstub_timeout,pty_handback}.sh`
- Fix: Add three negative drivers: `rt_fault_partial_drain.sh`
  (truncate state.bin to half its size mid-handoff),
  `rt_fault_disk_full.sh` (run on a size-capped tmpfs smaller than
  state size), `rt_fault_mmap_resize.sh` (truncate the shared mmap
  while vsim is mid-execution). Each asserts a clean diagnostic exit.
- Status: not-started

### F-T3.6 Determinism across re-runs

- Trigger: Run the same ELF twice; diff the drained state files.
- Breaks: No guarantee of byte-identical output. `reserved[]` bytes,
  CSR drain order, and FP rounding sources could vary. Any test using
  exact-equality assertion is flaky.
- Source: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` drain order; ABI reserved
  bytes
- Fix: Add an e2e test that runs the same fixture twice and asserts
  `sha256sum state1.bin == sha256sum state2.bin`. Audit drain path:
  zero-initialise `reserved[]` explicitly in the plugin and in
  StateDrain; serialise CSR writes in canonical CSR-number order.
- Status: not-started

### F-T3.7 Self-modifying code

- Trigger: JIT or workload writes to .text inside ROI.
- Breaks: Shared mmap is live so the write is visible immediately,
  but QEMU1 has cached the old insn in TCG and vsim's icache starts
  cold. Same binary -> different trace.
- Source: documented out-of-scope in `hybrid_plan.md` Section 2.5;
  not detected
- Fix: At orchestrator startup, parse the ELF for `.text` PHDRs and
  call `mprotect(..., PROT_READ)` on the corresponding mmap pages.
  Any write fault becomes a clean SIGSEGV with a diagnostic naming
  the offending PC. SMC stays out-of-scope but is now detected
  instead of silently corrupting traces.
- Status: not-started

### F-T3.8 GDB handshake timeout / zombie QEMU2

- Trigger: QEMU2 launches but its gdbstub does not respond within 5s,
  or responds then hangs mid-P-packet.
- Breaks: `qemu_handback::connect_loopback` may time out but the
  spawned QEMU2 child can be left as a zombie if the orchestrator
  has no SIGALRM watchdog.
- Source: `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`
- Fix: In `connect_loopback`, install a `setitimer`-based watchdog
  before the gdb handshake. On SIGALRM, `kill(child_pid, SIGKILL)`
  then `waitpid(child_pid, ..., 0)` to reap, then throw. RAII guard
  ensures reap happens on any throw path.
- Status: not-started

   for F-T3.1. Single gdbstub `g` packet at QEMU2 entry, memcmp
   against the drained `state.bin`.

   partially addresses F-T1.2 and F-T1.3 by establishing the
   ResumeDriver pattern for Tier-A and Tier-B CSRs.
3. **Promote `hybrid_plan.md` Phase 5 hardening to a tracked ROADMAP** -
   covers F-T1.2, F-T1.3, F-T1.4, F-T1.5, F-T2.1, F-T2.3, F-T2.5 in

4	// implementation-specific extensions), so vsim moves v0..v31 by executing a
5	// vle8.v/vse8.v sweep on the halted hart through the Program Buffer (see

7	// StateDrain at drain). That sweep loads/stores a fixed scratch region of

14	//     the gdbstub P packets.
15	//

17	// transport code, only the enter_vsim / exit_vsim markers. rt_c_v_regs.c is
18	// the reference fixture.

33	{
34	
35	// Reserved scratch slot inside the shared mmap. Sits well above the C
36	// runtime's _stack (rt_c.ld places it at RAM_BASE + 0x700000), giving the
37	// stack ~9 MiB of headroom before colliding with this 2 KiB region. On
38	// `-M andes_ae350` RAM is at 0x00000000 and the GPA is 0x00FF0000; on
39	// `-M virt` it would be 0x80FF0000. ResumeDriver/StateDrain stage the PB
40	// sweep's base pointer (x7) directly from this constant, so it is the single
41	// source of truth -- no fixture-side literal to keep in sync.
42	inline constexpr uint64_t kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000ull;
43	
44	// Total scratch bytes needed: 32 V regs × HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX. Sized to
45	// the maximum supported VLEN; the actual per-reg byte count is `vlenb`.
46	inline constexpr std::size_t kVScratchBytes =
47	  static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX;

52	// Translate scratch GPA into a byte offset inside a RAM span whose first
53	// byte sits at `ram_base`. Throws if the scratch region falls outside the
54	// supplied span (i.e. the caller passed a too-small RAM mapping).
55	inline auto scratch_offset(std::size_t ram_size, uint64_t ram_base)
56	  -> std::size_t
57	{
58	  if (kVScratchGpa < ram_base)
59	    throw std::runtime_error(
60	      "v_regfile_xfer: scratch GPA below RAM base");
61	  const auto off = static_cast<std::size_t>(kVScratchGpa - ram_base);
62	  if (off + kVScratchBytes > ram_size)

66	}

68	}  // namespace detail

73	inline void stage_v_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,

---

# Orchestrator Limitation Audit (read-only)

Scope note: SimPoint weight/cluster pairing and the `estimated_cycles` weighted-combine math live in the `hsim` driver (`_read_simpoint_phases`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline` - referenced by `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_hsim_simpoint_pairing.py`), NOT in the 8 audited files. Category 7 findings below are limited to what these 8 files actually contain (slice-index parsing, archive write, 0-step handling).

Ranked most severe (silent wrong results) first.

---

## SILENT CORRUPTION (wrong results, no error)

### 1. `priv` (privilege mode) is drained but never restored to QEMU2
- **File:line**: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:271-319` (the entire `apply_state`); field defined `abi.py:37`
- **Trigger**: any workload whose ROI ends in a privilege mode other than the QEMU2 reset default (e.g. drained while in S-mode or U-mode).
- **Symptom**: silent wrong result. QEMU2 continues in its reset privilege level, so privilege-sensitive instructions, trap delegation, and memory permission checks behave differently than the drained CPU. No error raised.
- **Evidence**: `apply_state` writes GPRs, pc, FPRs, the `_CSR_NAMES_AND_ATTRS` list, PMP, and V-state - `priv` appears nowhere. The struct carries it:
  ```python
  ("priv", ctypes.c_uint64),
  ```

### 2. `vlenb` is never written back to QEMU2
- **File:line**: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:307-319`
- **Trigger**: any V-extension workload where QEMU2's reset `vlenb` differs from the drained one (or just relying on it being authoritative). `vlenb` is part of the drained V-CSR set per the ABI.
- **Symptom**: silent corruption of vector length interpretation if QEMU2's VLEN default ever diverges from the drained value; `vlenb` is used to slice `vreg` bytes on write but its own register is never restored.
- **Evidence**: the V block writes `vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, vtype, vl` and the `v0..v31` data, but not `vlenb`:
  ```python
  _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, "vtype",  state.vtype)
  _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, "vl",     state.vl)
  vbytes = int(state.vlenb)
  ```

### 3. V-state silently skipped when `vlenb` is out of `(0, 64]` even though FLAG_V is set
- **File:line**: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:307`
- **Trigger**: a drained state with `HYBRID_FLAG_V` set but `vlenb == 0` (V enabled, vector unit reset/untouched in ROI) or `vlenb > HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX`.
- **Symptom**: silent corruption - the entire vector register file and all V-CSRs are skipped with no warning; QEMU2 keeps its reset V-state. The `&&` short-circuits the whole block instead of erroring on an inconsistent (FLAG_V set, vlenb invalid) state.
- **Evidence**:
  ```python
  if state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_V and 0 < state.vlenb <= HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX:
  ```

### 4. Per-CSR restore is silently skipped when the stub does not advertise the name
- **File:line**: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:251-258` (`_try_write_u64`), called at `299-305`
- **Trigger**: a QEMU build whose feature XML omits any of `medeleg/mideleg/mip/mie/satp/mscratch/...` (per-build CSR variation, which the docstring at `278-280` explicitly tolerates), or a name mismatch (e.g. stub names it differently).
- **Symptom**: silent corruption. That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value; `medeleg/mideleg` affecting trap routing, `satp` affecting address translation, `mie/mip` affecting interrupts - all silently wrong with zero diagnostics.
- **Evidence**: missing name returns early, no log:
  ```python
  reg = reg_map.get(name)
  if reg is None:
      return
  ```
  (Note: GPRs x1..x31 and `pc` are hard-failed instead - only the CSR/PMP/V path is silently skipped. The asymmetry is the hazard.)

### 5. P-packet value is unconditionally truncated/padded to 8 bytes
- **File:line**: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:84-87` (`encode_p_body`)
- **Trigger**: restoring `v0..v31` uses `_try_write_bytes` (variable length, OK), but every scalar CSR and GPR goes through `encode_p_body`, which forces exactly 8 bytes. On RV64 GPRs/CSRs that is correct; the limitation is it is hard-wired to 64-bit with no width from `reg_map`.
- **Symptom**: any register the stub expects at a non-8-byte width (e.g. a 4-byte CSR a future build advertises) is sent the wrong byte count; QEMU may reject the P packet (`RuntimeError`) or silently mis-store.
- **Evidence**:
  ```python
  le = value.to_bytes(8, "little", signed=False)
  ```

---

## HANG / CRASH

### 6. gdbstub RECV_TIMEOUT (10s) too short for long ROI; raises mid-restore
- **File:line**: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:135` (`RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0`), and `runner.py:384` passes `timeout_sec=10.0` to `restore_and_continue`
- **Trigger**: QEMU2 slow to answer a `qXfer` or P-packet under heavy host load, or a large feature-XML discovery (`fetch_feature_xml` loops). 10s is hard-coded and not derived from `spawn_timeout`.
- **Symptom**: `socket.timeout` inside `Session._recv_byte`/`send_command`. In `_qemu_resume_to_end` the generic `except Exception` (runner.py:389) kills QEMU2 and re-raises - the resume crashes rather than completing.
- **Evidence**:
  ```python
  RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0
  ```

### 7. `cont()` returns after only consuming the ACK - QEMU2 exit code race
- **File:line**: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:155-157`
- **Trigger**: every resume-to-end. `cont()` sends `$c#..`, reads one `+`, returns. The runner then calls `_wait(proc, timeout)` to harvest the exit code (runner.py:393).
- **Symptom**: not a bug per se, but the design relies on `proc.wait`; if QEMU2 hangs after continue (workload infinite loop, missing semihosting exit), the only backstop is `_wait`'s `timeout`, which on expiry kills QEMU2 and raises `TimeoutExpired` - the run dies rather than reporting a clean failure code.
- **Evidence**:
  ```python
  def cont(self) -> None:
      self._send_raw(encode_packet(b"c"))
      self._expect_ack()
  ```

### 8. RSP notifications (`%`) and run-length encoding (`*`) are not handled

### 14. Drain/resume child processes leak on timeout in `_wait` re-raise paths
- **File:line**: `tools/orchestrator/runner.py:176-182` (`_wait`)

- **File:line**: `tools/orchestrator/mmap_owner.py:51-64`

def discover_reg_map(sess: Session) -> dict[str, int]:
    reg_map: dict[str, int] = {}
    target_xml = fetch_feature_xml(sess, "target.xml")
    counter = [0]
    for annex in parse_target_xml(target_xml):
        annex_xml = fetch_feature_xml(sess, annex)
        parse_feature_xml(annex_xml, reg_map, counter)
    return reg_map


def _try_write_u64(sess: Session, reg_map: dict[str, int],
                   name: str, value: int) -> None:
    reg = reg_map.get(name)
    if reg is None:
        return
    reply = sess.send_command(encode_p_body(reg, value))
    if reply != b"OK":
        raise RuntimeError(f"P packet for {name} replied {reply!r}")


def _try_write_bytes(sess: Session, reg_map: dict[str, int],
                     name: str, data: bytes) -> None:
    reg = reg_map.get(name)
    if reg is None:
        return
    reply = sess.send_command(encode_p_body_bytes(reg, data))
    if reply != b"OK":
        raise RuntimeError(f"P packet for {name} replied {reply!r}")


def apply_state(sess: Session, reg_map: dict[str, int],
                state: HybridStateV1) -> None:
    """Write all architectural state into QEMU 2 via P packets.

    Order: GPRs x1..x31 by hard-coded regnum 1..31 (the RISC-V GDB CPU
    feature pins x0..x31 at 0..31 by spec), PC by reg_map["pc"] lookup
    (alternate stubs / future feature XML may place PC at any regnum so
    the hardcoded 32 is unsafe), then FPRs/M-CSRs/PMP/V-state by name
    lookup (silently skipped if QEMU's stub does not advertise that
    name - tolerates per-build CSR variation).
    """
    # x1..x31 (skip x0/zero, hard-wired) by fixed regnum.
    for i in range(1, 32):
        reply = sess.send_command(encode_p_body(i, state.gpr[i]))
        if reply != b"OK":
            raise RuntimeError(f"P packet for x{i} replied {reply!r}")
    pc_reg = reg_map.get("pc")
    if pc_reg is None:
        raise RuntimeError("apply_state: stub did not advertise 'pc' in "
                           "feature XML; refusing to guess regnum")
    reply = sess.send_command(encode_p_body(pc_reg, state.pc))
    if reply != b"OK":
        raise RuntimeError(f"P packet for pc (reg {pc_reg}) replied {reply!r}")

    if state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_FP:
        for i in range(32):
            _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, _FPR_NAMES[i], state.fpr[i])

    for name, attr in _CSR_NAMES_AND_ATTRS:
        _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, name, getattr(state, attr))

    for i in range(HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM):
        _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, f"pmpcfg{i}", state.pmpcfg[i])
    for i in range(HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM):
        _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, f"pmpaddr{i}", state.pmpaddr[i])

    if state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_V and 0 < state.vlenb <= HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX:
        _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, "vstart", state.vstart)
        _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, "vxsat",  state.vxsat)
        _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, "vxrm",   state.vxrm)
        _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, "vcsr",   state.vcsr)
        _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, "vtype",  state.vtype)
        _try_write_u64(sess, reg_map, "vl",     state.vl)
        vbytes = int(state.vlenb)
        vreg_buf = bytes(state.vreg)
        for i in range(32):
            base = i * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX
            _try_write_bytes(sess, reg_map, f"v{i}",
                             vreg_buf[base:base + vbytes])

    sess = Session(sock)
    try:
        reg_map = discover_reg_map(sess)
        apply_state(sess, reg_map, state)
        sess.cont()

"""Python ctypes mirror of `include/hybrid/state_abi.h::hybrid_state_v1`.

The C ABI is the wire contract between QEMU plugin, vsim, and the
orchestrator. This module mirrors it in ctypes so the orchestrator can
read and validate state files written by either CPU model.

Field offsets and the total struct size are asserted at import time
against the constants codified in `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`.
If a future ABI change forgets to update one side, importing this
module fails loudly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import struct
from pathlib import Path

HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC: int = 0x42594841
HYBRID_STATE_VERSION: int = 1

HYBRID_FLAG_RV64: int = 1 << 0
HYBRID_FLAG_FP: int = 1 << 1
HYBRID_FLAG_V: int = 1 << 2

HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX: int = 64
HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM: int = 16
HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM: int = 64


class HybridStateV1(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [
        ("magic", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("version", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("flags", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("hart_id", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("pc", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("priv", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("gpr", ctypes.c_uint64 * 32),
        ("fpr", ctypes.c_uint64 * 32),
        ("mstatus", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mepc", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mtvec", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mcause", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mtval", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mscratch", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("medeleg", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mideleg", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mip", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mie", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mcycle", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("minstret", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("satp", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("pmpcfg", ctypes.c_uint64 * HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM),
        ("pmpaddr", ctypes.c_uint64 * HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM),
        ("vstart", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vtype", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vl", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vlenb", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vreg", ctypes.c_uint8 * (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)),
        ("vxsat", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vxrm", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vcsr", ctypes.c_uint64),
        # F13: warmup-window snapshot. Drain-only; zero when disabled.
        ("mcycle_at_measure_start", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("minstret_at_measure_start", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("reserved", ctypes.c_uint8 * 216),
    ]


HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE: int = ctypes.sizeof(HybridStateV1)


# Mirror state_abi_check.h. If any of these fire, the ctypes layout has
# drifted from C and the wire format would be silently mis-parsed.
def _check_layout() -> None:
    expected: dict[str, int] = {
        "magic": 0,
        "version": 4,
        "flags": 8,
        "hart_id": 12,
        "pc": 16,
        "priv": 24,
        "gpr": 32,
        "fpr": 288,
        "mstatus": 544,
        "mepc": 552,
        "mtvec": 560,
        "mcause": 568,
        "mtval": 576,
        "mscratch": 584,
        "medeleg": 592,
        "mideleg": 600,
        "mip": 608,
        "mie": 616,
        "mcycle": 624,
        "minstret": 632,
        "satp": 640,
        "pmpcfg": 648,
        "pmpaddr": 776,
        "vstart": 1288,
        "vtype": 1296,
        "vl": 1304,
        "vlenb": 1312,
        "vreg": 1320,
    }
    vreg_end = 1320 + 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX
    expected["vxsat"] = vreg_end
    expected["vxrm"] = vreg_end + 8
    expected["vcsr"] = vreg_end + 16
    expected["mcycle_at_measure_start"] = vreg_end + 24
    expected["minstret_at_measure_start"] = vreg_end + 32
    expected["reserved"] = vreg_end + 40
    for name, want in expected.items():
        got = getattr(HybridStateV1, name).offset
        if got != want:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"hybrid_state_v1.{name} offset mismatch: C={want} ctypes={got}"
            )
    want_size = vreg_end + 256
    if HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE != want_size:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"sizeof(hybrid_state_v1) mismatch: "
            f"C={want_size} ctypes={HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE}"
        )


_check_layout()


def validate_state_file(path: str | Path) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError if `path` is not a valid v1 hybrid state file.

    Checks (in order):
      - file size equals `sizeof(hybrid_state_v1)`
      - magic header equals `HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC`
      - version equals `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION`

    Does not validate field semantics (e.g. flag bit consistency, PC
    sanity); that is the consumer's responsibility.
    """
    p = Path(path)
    raw = p.read_bytes()
    if len(raw) != HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{p}: size {len(raw)} != expected {HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE}"
        )
    magic, version = struct.unpack_from("<II", raw, 0)
    if magic != HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{p}: magic 0x{magic:08x} != expected 0x{HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:08x}"
        )
    if version != HYBRID_STATE_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{p}: version {version} != expected {HYBRID_STATE_VERSION}"
        )

def _read_simpoint_phases(simpts: Path,
                          weights: Path) -> list[tuple[int, float]]:
    """B15: pair SimPoint's simpts <-> weights rows by cluster id.

    Each file row is `<value> <cluster_id>`. Positional pairing (zip) is
    fragile if a future SimPoint emits the two files in different
    orderings; pair by cluster id instead so the weighted CPI math is
    invariant to row order. Returns the (K, weight) pairs.
    """
    def _parse(path: Path, val_fn):
        rows = {}
        for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) < 2:
                continue
            rows[int(parts[1])] = val_fn(parts[0])
        return rows
    k_by_cluster = _parse(simpts, int)
    w_by_cluster = _parse(weights, float)
    if set(k_by_cluster) != set(w_by_cluster):
        raise ValueError(
            f"hsim: simpts/weights cluster id mismatch "
            f"(simpts={sorted(k_by_cluster)} vs weights={sorted(w_by_cluster)})")
    # Sort by cluster id for stable iteration; the sum is commutative
    # so this is purely for predictable human output.
    return [(k_by_cluster[c], w_by_cluster[c])
            for c in sorted(k_by_cluster)]


def _run_simpoint_pipeline(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                           interval: int, max_k: int,
                           vsim_icount: int, mmap_size: int) -> int:
    """Full SimPoint cycle estimator: profile -> cluster -> per-phase drain.

    Shared by `./hsim estimate` and `./hsim run --mode simpoint`. Always
    profiles to natural program exit (plugin atexit counter -> N_total).
    Returns 0 on success and prints `estimated_cycles=<int>` as the
    headline line.
    """
    # B16: explicit `--vsim-icount 0` is no longer silently coerced to
    # `interval`. The sentinel for the SimPoint-correct auto-default is
    # `None` (argparse omits the flag) or any negative value; an explicit
    # 0 is rejected to surface what the user actually requested instead
    # of producing a phase cycle figure for what they may have intended
    # as a no-op probe.
    if vsim_icount == 0:
        print("hsim: --vsim-icount=0 is not valid in --mode simpoint; "
              "omit the flag (uses --interval as auto-default) or pass "
              "an explicit positive value",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if vsim_icount is None or vsim_icount < 0:
        vsim_icount = interval

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="hsim-simpoint-") as tmpdir:
        tmp = Path(tmpdir)
        bbv = tmp / "profile.bb"
        simpts = tmp / "simpts"
        weights = tmp / "weights"

        rc, n_total = _run_drain_at_exit_profile(
            elf, artifacts, bbv, interval, mmap_size,
        )
        if rc != 0:
            return rc

        rc = cmd_cluster(argparse.Namespace(
            bbv=str(bbv), max_k=max_k,
            simpts=str(simpts), weights=str(weights), dry_run=False,
        ))
        if rc != 0:
            return rc

        try:
            pairs = _read_simpoint_phases(simpts, weights)
        except ValueError as exc:
            print(f"hsim: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        slice_indices = [K for K, _ in pairs]

        phases = []
        for K, w in pairs:
            print(f"[hsim simpoint] phase slice_at={K} weight={w:.3f}",
                  flush=True)
            try:
                # qemu_icount_fallback=0: slice_at is the primary trigger;
                # we no longer expose a profile-pass icount cap.
                mc_before, mc_after = _estimate_one_phase(
                    elf, artifacts, interval, K,
                    0, vsim_icount,
                    mmap_size=mmap_size,
                )
            except RuntimeError as exc:
                print(f"hsim: simpoint failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
            delta = mc_after - mc_before
            cpi = delta / vsim_icount if vsim_icount > 0 else 0.0
            phases.append({"K": K, "w": w, "delta": delta, "cpi": cpi})

        weighted_cpi = sum(p["w"] * p["cpi"] for p in phases)
        estimated_cycles = int(n_total * weighted_cpi)

        print(f"M4 profile: {len(slice_indices)} BBV rows ({bbv.name})")
        print(f"cluster: {len(phases)} phases")
        for p in phases:
            print(f"phase K={p['K']} w={p['w']:.3f} "
                  f"delta_mcycle={p['delta']} CPI={p['cpi']:.3f}")
        print(f"estimated_cycles={estimated_cycles}  "
              f"(N={n_total}, weighted_CPI={weighted_cpi:.3f})")
        return 0


def cmd_estimate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    elf = Path(args.elf)
    if not elf.is_absolute():
        elf = (Path.cwd() / elf).resolve()
    if not elf.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: ELF not found: {args.elf}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    artifacts = _resolve_artifacts()
    for label, path in artifacts.items():
        if not path.is_file():
            print(f"hsim: {label} not built -- run ./hsim build",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
    if not _SIMPOINT_BIN.is_file():
        print("hsim: simpoint not built -- run ./hsim build",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    return _run_simpoint_pipeline(
        elf=elf, artifacts=artifacts,
        interval=args.slice, max_k=args.max_k,
        vsim_icount=args.vsim_icount, mmap_size=args.mmap_size,
    )


# --- main -------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="hsim",
        description="End-user driver for the Andes hybrid simulator (QEMU + vsim).",
    )

# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. Written 2026-05-28 from a direct read of
the current code (not just the older audit notes).

How this file relates to the others:

- `docs/TODO.md` - the engineering fix backlog (failure modes `F-T*`). It is
  the *plan to fix*. This file is the *plain-English "do not do this" list*.
- `ROADMAP.md` - feature roadmap. Its bug-audit wave `B1-B20` is fully closed,
  so those are NOT limitations anymore. The open items live in `docs/TODO.md`.

Each entry below was checked against the code on 2026-05-28. The `Where`
line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.

---

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No system calls / semihosting
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

---

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 / phase 3 (the two QEMU
  legs). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears. (PMP IS restored to QEMU2 afterward, so the gap is
  the vsim window only.)
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained and restored to QEMU2, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
  PMP-static but not paging).

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through to QEMU2. Any
  trap-diagnostic logic after the handoff sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
  the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

---

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
  trigger boundary.
- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. On the QEMU2 side,
  `apply_state` never writes `priv` at all (it is in the struct at
  `abi.py:37` but absent from `gdbstub.py:271-319`). S/U code then raises
  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`, `gdbstub.py` apply_state.
- Status: OPEN.

### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
  shared memory.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption.
- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
  ELF size against it.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
  both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
  any aliased/device memory.
- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory. QEMU2
  device state then disagrees with vsim.
- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
- Status: OPEN.

---

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. The whole pipeline is hard-wired to one CPU

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU other than
  `andes-ax45mpv`, or any VLEN other than 512.
- What happens: the QEMU2 spawn passes `-machine andes_ae350` and
  `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` literally (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`).
  The V-register scratch address is the constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000`
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), which is only correct when RAM base is 0 (true
  for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt` where it would need 0x80FF0000).
  The shared-memory base defaults to 0 in `spawn.py`. Nothing parameterizes
  these per machine.
- Where: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:38-42`.
- Status: by design for now; blocks porting to another core.

### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
  or any future config change to VLEN.
- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0

- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
  immediate 0 or 1.
- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.

### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)

- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
  this gate must change together.
- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim estimate` run where you read
  the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
  (`hsim:1188-1193`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
     CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim:1122-1202` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

---

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. No value-level check that the handoff copied state correctly  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: those paths only assert exit code and PC range. A wrong
  register value passes silently. There is no `g`-packet readback compared
  against the drained state.
- Where: `hsim` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: OPEN. This is the cheapest high-value fix (see TODO.md "next moves").

### L16. CSR restore to QEMU2 is silently skipped if the stub omits the name

- When it bites: a QEMU build whose feature XML does not advertise some CSR
  (e.g. `medeleg`, `satp`, `mie`).
- What happens: GPRs and PC hard-fail if missing, but every CSR/PMP/V write
  goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns quietly when the name is not
  found (`gdbstub.py:251-258`). That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value with no
  warning. The asymmetry (hard-fail GPR vs silent-skip CSR) is the hazard.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:251-258`, used at `gdbstub.py:299-305`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L17. gdbstub handback uses a fixed 10 s timeout and a racy port pick

- When it bites: QEMU2 slow to answer under host load; or many parallel runs
  (the `JOBS=8` e2e runner) picking ports at the same time.
- What happens: `RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0` is hardcoded (`gdbstub.py:135`); a slow
  reply raises mid-restore and the run dies. `pick_free_port` binds port 0,
  reads the number, closes, then QEMU binds it later - a TOCTOU window where
  another process can grab the port (`spawn.py`, acknowledged in its
  comment). Wrong-port connect = hang until timeout.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:135`, `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
  with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
  path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror uses a native-endian
  `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:30`), so a BE host would mis-parse the body
  while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:30`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- A QEMU2 that launches but never answers the gdbstub can be left as a
  zombie (no SIGALRM watchdog around the handshake).
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

---

## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)

`CLAUDE.md` and parts of the architecture notes still describe
`verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` as the component that spawns QEMU2
and sends gdbstub P-packets. That file no longer exists - the QEMU2 spawn and
handback moved into the Python orchestrator (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` +
`gdbstub.py`) in commit `7c7bf30`. Anyone debugging the handback by following
the docs will look in the wrong place.

---

## Quick reference

| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |
|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------|
| L1  | No syscalls/semihosting in ROI          | blocker  | open   |
| L2  | PMP not restored to vsim                | high     | open   |
| L3  | Paging (satp) off in ROI                | high     | open   |
| L4  | Trap state lost across ROI              | high     | open   |
| L5  | LR/SC cannot cross handoff              | high     | open   |
| L6  | Privilege forced to M-mode              | high     | open   |
| L7  | 128 MB mmap, no bounds check            | medium   | open   |
| L8  | Single hart only                        | medium   | open   |
| L9  | MMIO in ROI not handled                 | medium   | open   |
| L10 | Hard-wired to andes_ae350 / ax45mpv     | medium   | by design |
| L11 | VLEN fixed at 512, mismatch silent      | medium   | open   |
| L12 | CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision             | low      | inherent |
| L13 | CSR marker must be 32-bit               | low      | documented |
| L14 | SimPoint estimate is approximate        | medium   | by design |
| L15 | No value-level handoff check            | medium   | open   |
| L16 | CSR restore silently skipped if missing | medium   | open   |
| L17 | Fixed gdbstub timeout + racy port       | low      | open   |
| L18 | Little-endian / same-arch only          | low      | by design |
| L19 | Determinism / drift / fault-injection   | low      | open   |

---

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No system calls / semihosting
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

---

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 / phase 3 (the two QEMU
  legs). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears. (PMP IS restored to QEMU2 afterward, so the gap is
  the vsim window only.)
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained and restored to QEMU2, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
  PMP-static but not paging).

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through to QEMU2. Any
  trap-diagnostic logic after the handoff sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
  the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

---

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
  trigger boundary.
- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. On the QEMU2 side,
  `apply_state` never writes `priv` at all (it is in the struct at
  `abi.py:37` but absent from `gdbstub.py:271-319`). S/U code then raises
  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`, `gdbstub.py` apply_state.
- Status: OPEN.

### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
  shared memory.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption.
- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
  ELF size against it.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
  both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
  any aliased/device memory.
- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory. QEMU2
  device state then disagrees with vsim.
- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
- Status: OPEN.

---

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. The whole pipeline is hard-wired to one CPU

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU other than
  `andes-ax45mpv`, or any VLEN other than 512.
- What happens: the QEMU2 spawn passes `-machine andes_ae350` and
  `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` literally (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`).
  The V-register scratch address is the constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000`
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), which is only correct when RAM base is 0 (true
  for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt` where it would need 0x80FF0000).
  The shared-memory base defaults to 0 in `spawn.py`. Nothing parameterizes
  these per machine.
- Where: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:38-42`.
- Status: by design for now; blocks porting to another core.

### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
  or any future config change to VLEN.
- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0

- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
  immediate 0 or 1.
- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.

### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)

- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
  this gate must change together.
- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim estimate` run where you read
  the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
  (`hsim:1188-1193`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
     CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim:1122-1202` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

---

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. No value-level check that the handoff copied state correctly  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: those paths only assert exit code and PC range. A wrong
  register value passes silently. There is no `g`-packet readback compared
  against the drained state.
- Where: `hsim` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: OPEN. This is the cheapest high-value fix (see TODO.md "next moves").

### L16. CSR restore to QEMU2 is silently skipped if the stub omits the name

- When it bites: a QEMU build whose feature XML does not advertise some CSR
  (e.g. `medeleg`, `satp`, `mie`).
- What happens: GPRs and PC hard-fail if missing, but every CSR/PMP/V write
  goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns quietly when the name is not
  found (`gdbstub.py:251-258`). That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value with no
  warning. The asymmetry (hard-fail GPR vs silent-skip CSR) is the hazard.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:251-258`, used at `gdbstub.py:299-305`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L17. gdbstub handback uses a fixed 10 s timeout and a racy port pick

- When it bites: QEMU2 slow to answer under host load; or many parallel runs
  (the `JOBS=8` e2e runner) picking ports at the same time.
- What happens: `RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0` is hardcoded (`gdbstub.py:135`); a slow
  reply raises mid-restore and the run dies. `pick_free_port` binds port 0,
  reads the number, closes, then QEMU binds it later - a TOCTOU window where
  another process can grab the port (`spawn.py`, acknowledged in its
  comment). Wrong-port connect = hang until timeout.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:135`, `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
  with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
  path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror uses a native-endian
  `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:30`), so a BE host would mis-parse the body
  while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:30`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- A QEMU2 that launches but never answers the gdbstub can be left as a
  zombie (no SIGALRM watchdog around the handshake).
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

---

## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)

`CLAUDE.md` and parts of the architecture notes still describe
`verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` as the component that spawns QEMU2
and sends gdbstub P-packets. That file no longer exists - the QEMU2 spawn and
handback moved into the Python orchestrator (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` +
`gdbstub.py`) in commit `7c7bf30`. Anyone debugging the handback by following
the docs will look in the wrong place.

---

We mostly shouldn't. Each limitation is a *structural gap in a code path* - a register that is never written, a check that doesn't exist. You can prove "PMP is dropped" by showing the resume code emits no PMP write, not by running a PMP workload end-to-end and watching it corrupt. Building QEMU + the vsim Docker image only proves emergent runtime behavior, which almost none of these need.

The repo is already built for this. Per CLAUDE.md, `src/hybrid/*.hpp` is header-only (C++20 + the ABI header, no SystemC/Verilator), and there are test doubles - `RecordingBus` for the DMI bus, a fake gdb session for the orchestrator. So each bug reproduces at its lowest layer in **seconds with plain g++/python, no Docker**.

Cheapest layer that exhibits each limitation:

| Layer (cost) | Tool | Limitations it proves |
|---|---|---|
| ABI / data (sec) | python `abi.py`, static_asserts | L11 VLEN, L18 endianness |
| vsim resume/drain (sec) | host g++ doctest + `RecordingBus` | L2 PMP, L3 satp, L4 trap CSRs, L6 (vsim side), L12 CSR collision, L13 marker width |
| orchestrator (sec) | pytest + fake gdb session | L6 (QEMU2 side), L11 vlenb gate, L15 no value check, L16 silent CSR skip, L17 timeout const |
| static/config (sec) | assert on `spawn.py` output | L10 hardwired CPU, L5 missing ABI field, L8 single-hart counter |
| full handoff (min, Docker) | `./hsim run` | L1 semihosting hang, L9 MMIO - the only truly *emergent* ones |

The payoff matches your TDD + compound-effect principle: each reproducer is a **RED test** for the eventual fix. When someone restores PMP, L2's test flips RED->GREEN and becomes a permanent regression guard. Building ELFs that run the full pipeline would give you slow, flaky demos instead of fast regression tests.

A few (L14 estimate accuracy, L19 determinism/drift) aren't defects or aren't "programs" - I'll mark those with a one-line repro recipe rather than force-fit code.

So the reframed plan: for each limitation, write the smallest failing test at the layer in the table, runnable in seconds, doubling as the fix's RED test. I'll actually run the cheap ones and capture the real output as proof.
